name: Fluffy Pancakes
steps: In a bowl, sift together flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
Make a well in the center and pour in the milk, egg, and melted butter; mix until smooth.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle over medium-high heat.
Pour or scoop the batter onto the griddle. Brown on both sides and serve hot.
funFact: Pancakes have been eaten for over 30,000 years — some of the earliest known grains found were pancake-like!

name: Avocado Toast
steps: Toast the bread to your desired crispiness.
Mash the avocado in a bowl with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Spread the mashed avocado on toast.
Sprinkle with chili flakes if desired.
funFact: Avocados are technically berries — and have more potassium than bananas!

name: Chicken Caesar Wrap
steps: In a bowl, mix chicken, lettuce, Caesar dressing, and Parmesan.
Spoon the mixture into tortillas.
Roll up tightly and slice in half.
Serve immediately or wrap for later.
funFact: Caesar salad was invented in Mexico by Italian-American chef Caesar Cardini.

name: Grilled Cheese Sandwich
steps: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
Place cheese between the unbuttered sides.
Grill in a skillet over medium heat until golden brown on both sides.
funFact: National Grilled Cheese Day is celebrated on April 12th in the US!

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
steps: Cook spaghetti according to package instructions.
In a pan, sauté onion and garlic, add beef and brown.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, herbs, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 30 minutes and serve over spaghetti.
funFact: Bolognese sauce actually originated in Bologna, Italy — and traditionally uses tagliatelle, not spaghetti!

name: Stir Fry Noodles
steps: Cook noodles and drain.
In a wok, heat sesame oil and sauté garlic and ginger.
Add vegetables and cook until tender.
Toss in noodles and soy sauce; stir fry for 2-3 minutes.
funFact: Stir-frying uses very high heat — it’s one of the fastest cooking methods!

name: Cheesecake Bites
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Mix cream cheese, sugar, egg, and vanilla.
Line muffin tin and press crust into base.
Fill with mixture and bake 15-18 mins.
Cool and chill before serving.
funFact: Cheesecake has been served since ancient Greece — even at the first Olympic Games!

name: Brownie Sundae
steps: Bake brownies and let them cool.
Cut into squares and place in a bowl.
Top with ice cream, syrup, and whipped cream.
Serve immediately.
funFact: Sundaes became popular in the 1890s as a legal workaround to Sunday soda bans!

name: Veggie Omelette
steps: Whisk eggs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil and cook veggies until soft.
Pour eggs over veggies and cook until set.
Fold and serve.
funFact: The largest omelette ever made weighed over 6 tons in Turkey in 2010!

name: Mac & Cheese
steps: Boil macaroni and drain.
Make a roux with butter and flour, then slowly add milk.
Stir in cheese until melted.
Mix in macaroni and bake or serve warm.
funFact: Thomas Jefferson popularized mac and cheese in the U.S. after visiting France!

name: Taco Salad
steps: Cook beef with taco seasoning.
Combine lettuce, cheese, chips, and beef.
Top with sour cream and serve.
funFact: Taco salad was first made popular in Texas during the 1960s Tex-Mex boom!

name: Lemon Bars
steps: Mix flour, butter, and powdered sugar; press into pan and bake at 350°F for 15 mins.
Whisk eggs, sugar, lemon juice, and flour; pour over crust.
Bake 20-25 mins. Cool and dust with powdered sugar.
funFact: Lemon bars became popular in American cookbooks in the 1960s — a true retro classic!

name: Quinoa Salad
steps: Rinse quinoa and cook with water according to package instructions.
Let quinoa cool, then combine with tomatoes, cucumber, and feta.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper, toss, and serve.
funFact: Quinoa is a complete protein, containing all nine essential amino acids!

name: Classic French Toast
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Dip bread slices in the mixture, coating both sides.
Fry in butter over medium heat until golden brown on both sides.
Serve with maple syrup.
funFact: French toast dates back to ancient Rome and is called 'pain perdu' in France, meaning 'lost bread'!

name: Caprese Skewers
steps: Thread a tomato, mozzarella ball, and basil leaf onto each skewer.
Arrange skewers on a platter.
Drizzle with balsamic glaze and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.
funFact: Caprese salad is named after the Italian island of Capri and features the colors of the Italian flag!
